Posted April 14, 2003
Analysis by Richard Cowan
See
2003: Major Developments Scheduled for Year. Things to Look Out For and Things to Look Forward To.

The following is a preview of my report to the NORML conference this week in San Francisco. On Friday I am chairing a panel on Developments in Canada and Europe.

Canada:
Immediately before the panel, Canadian Senator Pierre Claude Nolin, Chair, Senate Select Committee on Illegal Drugs will speak on " The Canadian Proposal to Legalize Marijuana. " His committee recommended full legalization.
See The Canadian Senate report

After his speech, Senator Nolin will join the panel and answer questions.

Today, the Canadian papers reported that when the Canadian parliament finally does move toward decriminalization it will be accompanied by a new multi-million dollar education campaign to keep the narks happy.

Unfortunately, it is Health Minister Anne McLellan, whose department is overseeing the new drug strategy. McLellan is a party line prohibitionist.
See
Canadian Health Minister Seeks Asylum In DEAland; Says Making Her Think About Medical Cannabis Constitutes Torture. In DC They Don't Allow That Sort of Thing. Thinking, That Is.

The program is not yet ready to take to the federal cabinet for approval before it is introduced to the Parliament. Prime Minister Chretien may yet decide to delay it again, but he leaves office next February.
See
Canadian Prime Minister Says He Has Been In Favor Of Decrim Since 1980. How Time Flies When You Are In Power. Possession Law Hostage to Medical Cannabis. Another Deadline On Taking Care of Patients.

Justice Minister Martin Cauchon is close to Paul Martin, who is generally expected to be the next PM, and is quoted as saying that the " education campaign " will stress that marijuana is still illegal and police will be instructed to be " more vigilant " in enforcing law.
See
Canadian Justice Minister Calls for National Debate On Cannabis Policies And Begins It By Debating Himself. Phony Decrim Bill May Be Used As Cover To Increase Penalties for Growing.

In short, I am not at all sure that decriminalization is a good idea in the Canadian context. Fortunately, the Canadian Supreme Court is hearing arguments against all of cannabis prohibition in early May, and is expect to rule around the first of the year.
See
Ontario Judge Prods Canadian Government On Medical Cannabis Program. Supreme Court Hearings On All Cannabis Prohibition Now Set For May. We Are Winning!

The Netherlands:
In Holland, the talks to form a coalition with the two largest parties, the Christian Democrats and the Social Democrats (Labor), just collapsed, which means that the present greatly weakened coalition of the Christian Democrats, the conservative VVD, and the Pim Fortuyn List will probably continue. The remaining PFL people are true to their late founder, and would oppose any strong move against the coffee shop system. In any case, the coffee shop regulations are set locally, so the national government is limited in what it can do without a Herculean effort which is beyond the capacity of the present group.
See
 Dutch Government Reconfirms Coffee Shop Policy. Drops Any Mention of Closing Border Shops. The Justice Minister Is Educating the Prime Minister.
and
 MarijuanaNews Reported It A Month Ago, But Now It's Official: Dutch Pharmacies Provide Medical cannabis Covered by Health Insurance.

Switzerland:
The IACM Bulletin reports that A commission of the Nationalrat (Swiss Lower House of Parliament) passed a bill that would change the narcotics act. Cannabis use is intended to become legal for private use by subjects above 16 years of age, but more expensive than today. A tax of 8 Swiss Francs (5.5 Euros) per gram with a THC content below 10% and 15 Francs (10 Euros) with a THC content between 10 and 15% is planned which is intended for use partly for addiction prevention purposes. The revision of the narcotics act will be discussed in the Nationalrat in May. (Source: SDA of 28 March 2003)

Such high taxes would be really dumb, because it will encourage a black market. Consequently, I really doubt that this will become the law. The Swiss are rarely dumb in financial matters.
See
Swiss Government Says Going Dutch Does NOT Violate Treaties. Implications for Other Countries, Especially Canada and UK. Plus Full Text of UN Nark Press Release.

The Czech Republic:
In late 1998, the Czech Parliament criminalized possessing more than a small amount of cannabis.
See
 New Czech Law Will Allow 20 Joints Comparable To DEAland Legal Medical Marijuana

However, at the time that they did that they also authorized a study of the consequences, and the easily predicable results are in. I am told that they are taking the report seriously, so there may be a debate on cannabis prohibition this year.

The UK:
Earlier this year, researchers from South Bank University and the National Addiction Centre reported that half the cannabis consumed in England and Wales is now home-grown. (Selling seeds is legal in the UK and there are a number of large seed companies there.) Heretofore it has been mostly smuggled hashish, and some smuggled Dutch weed.

Now the influential Joseph Rowntree Foundation is pushing to change the law for home-growers, pointing out that 243 people were jailed in 2000 for growing cannabis in England and Wales. (Scotland has a different system, but cannot legalize without London's approval)
See
De Facto Cannabis Decriminalization In Scotland? Is Crack Epidemic In Brixton the Fault of Cannabis Decriminalization? Or Is The UK Drugs Problem Just Part of Crises In Law

There is a wide range of consequences in the way different police forces treat growers.
See
Wide Range Of Consequences For People Caught with Cannabis in UK.

Some are charged with production - which has a mandatory seven-year sentence for a third conviction - while others opt for the lesser offence of cultivation.

Professor Mike Hough, a co-author of the report, A Growing Market, is quoted as saying, " If small-scale home cultivation attracted an on-the-spot warning rather than a caution or a court conviction, it is likely that more users would switch to growing their own and stop buying from dealers.

" Large minorities of young people use cannabis.

" It is essential to insulate them as much as possible from drug markets operated by dealers who sell not only cannabis but crack and heroin.

" As their profits from cannabis sales diminished, criminal entrepreneurs could be forced to abandon the cannabis market altogether. "

That is a nice thought, but like the proposed reclassification of cannabis, which is likely to be finally done later this year, this proposal would be great for the middleclass, but will do little for the poor.
See
UK Committee Will Endorse Reclassification " Decriminalization " By Another Name, But Says Real " Decriminalization " Would " Send the Wrong Message " Cannabis Equals Valium Is The Right Message?

The Brits ignore the Dutch, for reasons that are difficult to understand, but only by having something like the coffee shop system can they hope to really separate the cannabis market from hard drugs. In any case, it is unlikely that the rather authoritarian Blair government will act on these recommendations.

Generally speaking, the move away from cannabis prohibition continues in Canada and most of Europe, other than France and Sweden, but politicians have a remarkable capacity to make a mess of things, and cannabis policies are certainly no exception.
